column2: コミュニケーション英語 / Communication English
column3: Practice Communication English lessons and units.
column6: Practice common classroom and daily-life English sentences.
column9: Choose the best response: How are you doing today?
column11: It is next to the library.
column14: I am doing well, thank you.
column20: This is a common greeting. A short, polite answer about your condition is natural. Teachers can also introduce 'I'm OK' or 'I'm a little tired' as useful alternatives.

column2: コミュニケーション英語 / Communication English
column3: Practice Communication English lessons and units.
column6: Practice common classroom and daily-life English sentences.
column9: Fill in the blank: I usually _____ the bus to school.
column20: Take the bus' is the most common phrase. 'Catch the bus' is also natural when the meaning is getting on a bus at the right time.

column2: コミュニケーション英語 / Communication English
column3: Practice Communication English lessons and units.
column6: Practice common classroom and daily-life English sentences.
column9: Choose the sentence that is most natural.
column10: I have a part-time job on weekends.
column11: I have part-time job in weekends.
column12: I am have a part-time job on weekends.
column13: I do a part-time job at weekend every.
column14: I have a part-time job during weekends.
column15: I have a part-time job by weekends.
column16: I am part-time job have weekends.
column18: I have a part-time job on weekends.
column20: Use 'have a part-time job' and 'on weekends' for a regular weekend activity. This example is useful for everyday conversation practice without asking students for personal details.

column2: コミュニケーション英語 / Communication English
column3: Practice Communication English lessons and units.
column6: Practice common classroom and daily-life English sentences.
column9: Fill in the blank: Could you _____ me your eraser for a moment?
column20: Lend me your eraser' means let me use it for a short time. 'Pass me your eraser' is also natural if the eraser is nearby.

column2: コミュニケーション英語 / Communication English
column3: Practice Communication English lessons and units.
column6: Practice common classroom and daily-life English sentences.
column9: Choose the best response: Thank you for your help.
column20: You're welcome' is a polite response to 'Thank you.' Teachers can also point out natural alternatives such as 'No problem' for casual situations.

column2: コミュニケーション英語 / Communication English
column3: Practice Communication English lessons and units.
column6: Practice common classroom and daily-life English sentences.
column9: Fill in the blank: I am looking _____ my phone. Have you seen it?
column20: The phrase 'look for' means to try to find something. This is different from 'look at,' which means to direct your eyes toward something.

column2: コミュニケーション英語 / Communication English
column3: Practice Communication English lessons and units.
column6: Practice common classroom and daily-life English sentences.
column9: Choose the polite way to make a request.
column10: Could you speak a little more slowly, please?
column14: Could you please speak a little more slowly?
column17: You must speak slowly for me.
column18: Could you speak a little more slowly, please?
column19: Could you please speak a little more slowly?
column20: Could you ... please?' and 'Could you please ...?' are polite request patterns. Both correct choices ask someone to speak more slowly in a respectful way.

column2: コミュニケーション英語 / Communication English
column3: Practice Communication English lessons and units.
column6: Practice common classroom and daily-life English sentences.
column9: Fill in the blank: I was absent _____ school yesterday because I had a fever.
column20: Use 'absent from school' to explain that someone did not attend school. The reason in this sentence is general and does not require personal information.

column2: コミュニケーション英語 / Communication English
column3: Practice Communication English lessons and units.
column6: Practice common classroom and daily-life English sentences.
column9: Choose the best sentence for giving an opinion.
column10: I think this idea is useful.
column11: I am think this idea useful.
column18: I think this idea is useful.
column20: Use 'I think ...' followed by a complete sentence. This pattern helps students express opinions in pair work and short presentations.

column2: コミュニケーション英語 / Communication English
column3: Practice Communication English lessons and units.
column6: Practice common classroom and daily-life English sentences.
column9: True or false: "You're welcome" is a natural response to "Thank you."
column20: You're welcome' is a polite and natural answer after someone says 'Thank you.' Students can also learn casual responses such as 'No problem.'

column2: コミュニケーション英語 / Communication English
column3: Practice Communication English lessons and units.
column6: Practice useful English for classes, clubs, homework, and school events.
column9: Choose the best response: May I borrow your notes after class?
column10: Sure, but please return them tomorrow.
column11: I usually eat lunch at noon.
column12: It is next to the station.
column14: Of course. Please bring them back tomorrow.
column15: I walk to school every morning.
column16: The station is very busy today.
column17: No, this is not my club.
column18: Sure, but please return them tomorrow.
column20: The question asks for permission to borrow something. A natural response gives permission and explains when the notes should be returned.

column2: コミュニケーション英語 / Communication English
column3: Practice Communication English lessons and units.
column6: Practice useful English for classes, clubs, homework, and school events.
column9: Fill in the blank: I have to _____ my homework before club practice.
column20: Both 'finish my homework' and 'do my homework' are common school expressions. 'Finish' emphasizes completing the work.

column2: コミュニケーション英語 / Communication English
column3: Practice Communication English lessons and units.
column6: Practice useful English for classes, clubs, homework, and school events.
column9: Choose the sentence that correctly asks about a test schedule.
column20: Use 'When is ...?' to ask about the time or date of an event. This pattern can be reused for meetings, club activities, and deadlines.

column2: コミュニケーション英語 / Communication English
column3: Practice Communication English lessons and units.
column6: Practice useful English for classes, clubs, homework, and school events.
column9: Fill in the blank: Our school festival is _____ Saturday.
column20: Use 'on' with days of the week, such as 'on Monday' or 'on Saturday.' Use 'at' for clock times and 'in' for months or years.

column2: コミュニケーション英語 / Communication English
column3: Practice Communication English lessons and units.
column6: Practice useful English for classes, clubs, homework, and school events.
column9: What does 'assignment' mean in a school context?
column20: In school English, an 'assignment' is work a teacher asks students to complete, such as homework, a worksheet, or a short project.

column2: コミュニケーション英語 / Communication English
column3: Practice Communication English lessons and units.
column6: Practice useful English for classes, clubs, homework, and school events.
column9: Fill in the blank: Could you _____ that again, please?
column20: Use 'Could you say that again?' or 'Could you repeat that?' when you did not hear or understand something. Both are polite classroom English.

column2: コミュニケーション英語 / Communication English
column3: Practice Communication English lessons and units.
column6: Practice useful English for classes, clubs, homework, and school events.
column9: Choose the best sentence for explaining why you were late to class.
column10: I'm sorry I'm late. My train was delayed.
column11: I'm sorry I'm late. I will eat dinner.
column12: I'm sorry I'm late. The library is quiet.
column13: I'm sorry I'm late. This pencil is mine.
column18: I'm sorry I'm late. My train was delayed.
column20: This sentence gives a polite apology and a clear reason. It is useful in Japan because train delays are a common, realistic situation.

column2: コミュニケーション英語 / Communication English
column3: Practice Communication English lessons and units.
column6: Practice useful English for classes, clubs, homework, and school events.
column9: Fill in the blank: We are preparing _____ the speech contest.
column20: The phrase is 'prepare for' an event, test, contest, or activity. Students can practice it with 'prepare for a test' or 'prepare for a presentation.'

column2: コミュニケーション英語 / Communication English
column3: Practice Communication English lessons and units.
column6: Practice useful English for classes, clubs, homework, and school events.
column9: Choose the best question to ask a teacher for help.
column10: Could you explain this problem, please?
column14: Would you explain this problem, please?
column18: Could you explain this problem, please?
column20: Could you ... please?' is a polite way to ask a teacher or classmate for help. The verb 'explain' is followed by the thing you want to understand.

column2: コミュニケーション英語 / Communication English
column3: Practice Communication English lessons and units.
column6: Practice useful English for classes, clubs, homework, and school events.
column9: True or false: "May I borrow your notes?" is a polite classroom request.
column20: May I ...?' is a polite way to ask permission in a classroom. Asking to borrow notes is a natural school-life situation.

column2: コミュニケーション英語 / Communication English
column3: Practice Communication English lessons and units.
column6: Practice practical English for trips, stations, directions, and asking for help.
column9: Choose the best question when you want to find the nearest station.
column10: Excuse me, where is the nearest station?
column11: Excuse me, what time do you eat breakfast?
column12: Excuse me, do you have math homework?
column13: Excuse me, is this your notebook?
column14: Excuse me, how can I get to the nearest station?
column15: Excuse me, is your homework finished?
column16: Excuse me, what club are you in?
column17: Excuse me, where is my math class?
column18: Excuse me, where is the nearest station?
column20: Use 'Where is ...?' to ask for the location of a place. 'Excuse me' makes the question polite when speaking to someone you do not know.

column2: コミュニケーション英語 / Communication English
column3: Practice Communication English lessons and units.
column6: Practice practical English for trips, stations, directions, and asking for help.
column9: Fill in the blank: Turn _____ at the traffic light.
column20: Both 'turn left' and 'turn right' are natural direction phrases. Teachers can have students point or draw a simple map when practicing.

column2: コミュニケーション英語 / Communication English
column3: Practice Communication English lessons and units.
column6: Practice practical English for trips, stations, directions, and asking for help.
column9: What does 'one-way ticket' mean?
column20: A 'one-way ticket' is a ticket for travel in one direction only. A 'round-trip ticket' is 往復切符.

column2: コミュニケーション英語 / Communication English
column3: Practice Communication English lessons and units.
column6: Practice practical English for trips, stations, directions, and asking for help.
column9: Fill in the blank: How long does it _____ to get to Kyoto by train?
column20: Use 'How long does it take to ...?' to ask about the amount of time needed. This is useful for travel and commuting conversations.

column2: コミュニケーション英語 / Communication English
column3: Practice Communication English lessons and units.
column6: Practice practical English for trips, stations, directions, and asking for help.
column9: Choose the best response: Is this train going to Tokyo?
column10: Yes, it is. It stops at Tokyo Station.
column11: Yes, I go to school by bike.
column18: Yes, it is. It stops at Tokyo Station.
column20: The question asks about the train's destination, so the best answer confirms where the train goes. 'Going to' is a natural phrase for destinations.

column2: コミュニケーション英語 / Communication English
column3: Practice Communication English lessons and units.
column6: Practice practical English for trips, stations, directions, and asking for help.
column9: Fill in the blank: The museum is next _____ the post office.
column20: The phrase 'next to' means beside or very close to another place. It is a basic but important phrase for giving directions.

column2: コミュニケーション英語 / Communication English
column3: Practice Communication English lessons and units.
column6: Practice practical English for trips, stations, directions, and asking for help.
column9: Choose the polite way to ask someone to take your photo while traveling.
column10: Could you take a picture of us, please?
column14: Would you take a picture of us, please?
column18: Could you take a picture of us, please?
column20: Could you ... please?' is a polite request, and 'take a picture of us' is the natural phrase when asking someone to use your camera or phone.

column2: コミュニケーション英語 / Communication English
column3: Practice Communication English lessons and units.
column6: Practice practical English for trips, stations, directions, and asking for help.
column9: Fill in the blank: We got _____ the bus at the city hall stop.
column20: Use 'get off' when leaving a bus, train, or plane. Use 'get on' when boarding a bus, train, or plane.

column2: コミュニケーション英語 / Communication English
column3: Practice Communication English lessons and units.
column6: Practice practical English for trips, stations, directions, and asking for help.
column9: Choose the best sentence for asking about a train platform.
column10: Which platform does the train leave from?
column12: This platform is my favorite food.
column13: When does the platform eat lunch?
column18: Which platform does the train leave from?
column20: Use 'Which platform does the train leave from?' to ask where to board a train. This is useful at large stations.

column2: コミュニケーション英語 / Communication English
column3: Practice Communication English lessons and units.
column6: Practice practical English for trips, stations, directions, and asking for help.
column9: True or false: "Excuse me, where is the nearest station?" is a natural way to ask for directions.
column20: Excuse me' makes the question polite, and 'Where is the nearest station?' clearly asks for a location.

column2: 論理・表現 / Logic and Expression
column3: Practice Logic and Expression lessons and units.
column6: Practice giving clear opinions with polite and useful expressions.
column9: Choose the best phrase to give your opinion politely.
column10: I think school uniforms are useful.
column18: I think school uniforms are useful.
column20: I think ...' is a clear and polite way to begin an opinion. The sentence also has a complete subject and verb.

column2: 論理・表現 / Logic and Expression
column3: Practice Logic and Expression lessons and units.
column6: Practice giving clear opinions with polite and useful expressions.
column9: Fill in the blank: In my _____, learning English is important.
column20: In my opinion' is a common expression for giving an idea. 'In my view' is also acceptable.

column2: 論理・表現 / Logic and Expression
column3: Practice Logic and Expression lessons and units.
column6: Practice giving clear opinions with polite and useful expressions.
column9: True or false: "I agree with you" is a natural way to show that you have the same opinion.
column20: I agree with you' directly and naturally shows that your opinion is the same as another person's opinion.

column2: 論理・表現 / Logic and Expression
column3: Practice Logic and Expression lessons and units.
column6: Practice giving clear opinions with polite and useful expressions.
column9: Choose the best sentence to disagree politely.
column10: I see your point, but I have a different opinion.
column13: Different opinion I have but see.
column14: I disagree because my lunch is cold.
column16: I see point but different have.
column18: I see your point, but I have a different opinion.
column20: I see your point, but ...' is a polite way to disagree because it first recognizes the other person's idea.

column2: 論理・表現 / Logic and Expression
column3: Practice Logic and Expression lessons and units.
column6: Practice giving clear opinions with polite and useful expressions.
column9: Fill in the blank: I _____ that group work helps students learn from each other.
column20: I believe that ...' and 'I think that ...' are useful patterns for stating an opinion with a full sentence after 'that.'

column2: 論理・表現 / Logic and Expression
column3: Practice Logic and Expression lessons and units.
column6: Practice giving reasons and examples to support opinions.
column9: Choose the best connector for giving a reason: I like reading books _____ they help me learn new ideas.
column20: Because' introduces a reason. The second part explains why the speaker likes reading books.

column2: 論理・表現 / Logic and Expression
column3: Practice Logic and Expression lessons and units.
column6: Practice giving reasons and examples to support opinions.
column9: Fill in the blank: I was absent _____ I had a fever.
column20: Because' and 'since' can introduce a reason. Both fit this simple explanation.

column2: 論理・表現 / Logic and Expression
column3: Practice Logic and Expression lessons and units.
column6: Practice giving reasons and examples to support opinions.
column9: True or false: A good reason should connect clearly to the opinion it supports.
column20: A reason is stronger when it clearly explains why the opinion makes sense.

column2: 論理・表現 / Logic and Expression
column3: Practice Logic and Expression lessons and units.
column6: Practice giving reasons and examples to support opinions.
column9: Choose the sentence that gives both an opinion and a reason.
column10: I think breakfast is important because it gives us energy.
column13: I went to school after breakfast.
column18: I think breakfast is important because it gives us energy.
column20: This sentence states an opinion, 'breakfast is important,' and supports it with the reason 'because it gives us energy.'

column2: 論理・表現 / Logic and Expression
column3: Practice Logic and Expression lessons and units.
column6: Practice giving reasons and examples to support opinions.
column9: Fill in the blank: For this _____, we should start the project early.
column20: For this reason' connects the previous idea to a conclusion or suggestion.

column2: 語彙 / Vocabulary
column3: Practice Vocabulary lessons and units.
column6: Practice useful vocabulary for classroom objects, actions, and places.
column9: What does "dictionary" mean in Japanese?
column20: A dictionary is a book or app used to check the meaning, spelling, or pronunciation of words.

column2: 語彙 / Vocabulary
column3: Practice Vocabulary lessons and units.
column6: Practice useful vocabulary for classroom objects, actions, and places.
column9: Fill in the blank: Please write your answer on the _____.
column20: Board,' 'blackboard,' and 'whiteboard' are all common classroom words for the place where teachers and students write for the class.

column2: 語彙 / Vocabulary
column3: Practice Vocabulary lessons and units.
column6: Practice useful vocabulary for classroom objects, actions, and places.
column9: True or false: A notebook is something students can write notes in.
column20: Students use notebooks to write class notes, answers, and ideas.

column2: 語彙 / Vocabulary
column3: Practice Vocabulary lessons and units.
column6: Practice useful vocabulary for classroom objects, actions, and places.
column9: Choose the word that means 「提出する」.
column20: Submit' means to hand in homework, a report, or another assignment to a teacher.

column2: 語彙 / Vocabulary
column3: Practice Vocabulary lessons and units.
column6: Practice useful vocabulary for classroom objects, actions, and places.
column9: Fill in the blank: I forgot my _____, so I cannot draw a straight line.
column20: A ruler is used to measure length and draw straight lines.

column2: 語彙 / Vocabulary
column3: Practice Vocabulary lessons and units.
column6: Practice useful vocabulary for transportation, places, and travel situations.
column9: What does "passport" mean in Japanese?
column20: A passport is an official document used when traveling to another country.

column2: 語彙 / Vocabulary
column3: Practice Vocabulary lessons and units.
column6: Practice useful vocabulary for transportation, places, and travel situations.
column9: Fill in the blank: We need to buy a train _____ before we get on the train.
column20: A ticket shows that you have paid to ride a train, bus, or other transportation.

column2: 語彙 / Vocabulary
column3: Practice Vocabulary lessons and units.
column6: Practice useful vocabulary for transportation, places, and travel situations.
column9: True or false: "Luggage" means bags or suitcases that people take when they travel.
column20: Luggage is the general word for travel bags and suitcases.

column2: 語彙 / Vocabulary
column3: Practice Vocabulary lessons and units.
column6: Practice useful vocabulary for transportation, places, and travel situations.
column9: Choose the word that means 「到着する」.
column20: Arrive' means to reach a place. 'Depart' means to leave a place.

column2: 語彙 / Vocabulary
column3: Practice Vocabulary lessons and units.
column6: Practice useful vocabulary for transportation, places, and travel situations.
column9: Fill in the blank: The plane will _____ from Gate 12 at 9:30.
column20: Depart' and 'leave' both mean to go away from a place. They are common words in travel information.

column3: Practice Vocabulary lessons and units.
column6: Practice vocabulary related to learning, school records, and self-improvement.

column20: average = ①平均の ②平均；平均点（例：the average score 平均点）

column6: Practice vocabulary related to learning, school records, and self-improvement.

column20: pupil = ①児童；生徒 ②瞳（例：a kindergarten pupil 幼稚園児）

column3: Practice Vocabulary lessons and units.

column20: remove = ①取り除く ②脱ぐ（例：remove a sentence 文を取り除く）

column3: Practice Vocabulary lessons and units.
column6: Practice vocabulary related to learning, school records, and self-improvement.

column20: reform = 改革する；改革（例：reform the system 制度を改革する）

column3: Practice Vocabulary lessons and units.
column6: Practice vocabulary related to learning, school records, and self-improvement.

column20: recover = 回復する（例：recover from the flu インフルエンザから回復する）
